slides.title: Four ways to move a shape
slides.prompt: Slide. Flip. Spin. Resize. Every transformation on your exam is one of these four.

children.content: SLIDE
FLIP
SPIN
RESIZE

slides.title: Match each move to its proper name

interaction.hint: Translation slides. Reflection flips. Rotation spins. Enlargement resizes.

config.prompt: Drag each name onto the move it describes.

config.successText: Enlargement scales the shape. The image is similar, not congruent.

slides.title: Naming the move isn't enough
slides.prompt: On your exam, you also have to describe the rule precisely. Different moves need different rules.

visual.content:
translation1 thing
reflection1 thing
rotation3 things
enlargement2 things

slides.title: Quick check before we dig in

interaction.hint: Three of these always keep length, angle, and orientation the same.

config.prompt: Which transformation does NOT change the size of the shape?

options.whyWrong: Enlargement is the one that changes size. The others all keep length and angle.

config.successText: Reflection, rotation and translation all keep every length and every angle. Only enlargement changes size.

slides.title: Translation: drag the triangle anywhere
slides.prompt: Every point slides the same amount. That amount is a column vector. Drag and watch.

interaction.hint: Drag the yellow tip until the column vector reads ⟨3, −2⟩.

config.prompt: Drag until the image lands on the pink outline. The shift you want is $\begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix}$.
config.successText: Every point moved by ⟨3, −2⟩. That's the entire description.

interaction.hint: Add the column vector to the coordinate: top to $x$, bottom to $y$.

config.prompt: A translation by $\begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix}$ moves the point $(1, 5)$ to...

options.whyWrong: You added $5 + 2$ instead of $5 + (-2)$. The bottom number is $-2$, so subtract.
You subtracted instead of added: $1 - 3 = -2$. The top number is positive $3$, so add.
You multiplied instead of added. A translation adds the vector, never multiplies.

config.successText: $(1 + 3,\ 5 + (-2)) = (4, 3)$. Top shifts $x$, bottom shifts $y$.

interaction.hint: Negative x means LEFT. Positive y means UP.

config.prompt: Different vector: $\begin{pmatrix} -4 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}$. Left and up.
config.successText: Negatives flip direction. Other than that, same idea.

interaction.hint: Subtract: image minus object. The order matters.

config.prompt: A point $(2, -1)$ has been translated to $(-3, 4)$. The column vector is...

options.whyWrong: You did object minus image. Always image minus object.
You used the image coordinates as the vector. The vector is the SHIFT, not the destination.
Those are the object coordinates, not the shift.

config.successText: $(-3 - 2,\ 4 - (-1)) = (-5, 5)$. Image minus object, always.

interaction.hint: y-component is 0. Move ONLY along the x-axis.

config.prompt: Slide $\begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}$. The image stays at the same height.
config.successText: A zero component means no shift in that direction. Same exam logic.

interaction.hint: Add component by component. Order doesn't matter for two translations.

config.prompt: Translate by $\begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$ then by $\begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -4 \end{pmatrix}$. The single equivalent translation is...

options.whyWrong: You multiplied $2 \times 3$ on top. Translations add, never multiply.
You subtracted instead of added.
Top should be $2 + 3 = 5$, not $1$.

config.successText: Top: $2 + 3 = 5$. Bottom: $1 + (-4) = -3$. Two translations always collapse into one.

interaction.hint: Type first, then the rule.

config.prompt: Arrange the tiles into a proper exam answer.
config.successText: “Translation by $\begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix}$.” One word, one vector, full marks.

slides.title: Reflection: drag the mirror line
slides.prompt: Every point flips to the other side of a line. Drag the yellow handles to move the mirror.

interaction.hint: Reflecting in $y = x$ swaps the two coordinates: $(x, y) \to (y, x)$.

config.prompt: The point $(3, 5)$ reflected in $y = x$ becomes...

options.whyWrong: You flipped both signs. That's a $180°$ rotation, not a reflection in $y = x$.
Close: $y = -x$ would do that. But $y = x$ just swaps, doesn't flip signs.
That's a reflection in the $x$-axis. The mirror $y = x$ is the diagonal.

config.successText: Reflecting in $y = x$ just swaps the two coordinates. Quick rule for this mirror only.

interaction.hint: Reflecting in the $x$-axis ($y = 0$) flips the sign of $y$ only.

config.prompt: The point $(2, -4)$ reflected in the $x$-axis becomes...

options.whyWrong: That flips $x$, not $y$. That would be a reflection in the $y$-axis.
You flipped both signs. The $x$-axis only flips $y$.
That's a swap, which is the rule for $y = x$, not the $x$-axis.

config.successText: $(x, y) \to (x, -y)$. Only the $y$ flips when the mirror is the $x$-axis.

slides.title: Four mirrors, four swap rules
slides.prompt: Memorise these four. They cover almost every Cambridge reflection question.

visual.content:
\(y = 0\)  flip sign of \(y\)
\((x,y) \to (x,-y)\)
\(x = 0\)  flip sign of \(x\)
\((x,y) \to (-x,y)\)
\(y = x\)  swap the two
\((x,y) \to (y,x)\)
\(y = -x\)  swap and flip both
\((x,y) \to (-y,-x)\)

interaction.hint: Imagine folding the page along each line. Which one lands blue on pink?

config.prompt: The blue triangle was reflected to land on the pink. Which mirror did it?
config.contextHtml: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' style='display:block;width:100%;max-width:420px;height:auto;margin:0 auto;background:#0b1118;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #141e2a' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><defs><pattern id='gqm' width='30' height='30' patternUnits='userSpaceOnUse'><path d='M 30 0 L 0 0 0 30' fill='none' stroke='#1a3350' stroke-width='0.5' opacity='0.4'/></pattern></defs><rect width='320' height='200' fill='url(#gqm)'/><line x1='10' y1='100' x2='310' y2='100' stroke='#1a3350' stroke-width='0.5'/><line x1='160' y1='10' x2='160' y2='190' stroke='#1a3350' stroke-width='0.5'/><polygon points='60,140 60,80 110,110' fill='rgba(0,171,250,0.55)' stroke='#00abfa' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='220,40 160,40 190,90' fill='rgba(255,70,112,0.55)' stroke='#ff4670' stroke-width='1.5'/></svg>

options.whyWrong: The $x$-axis flips top-bottom only. Pink would still be on the left.
The $y$-axis flips left-right only. Pink would still be near the bottom.
$y = -x$ sends the image to the bottom-right, not the top.

config.successText: $y = x$ is the diagonal through the origin going up-right.

slides.title: Words don't earn marks. Equations do.

config.prompt: Two students describe the same reflection. Which one earns the mark?

options.whyWrong: Words don't earn the mark. The examiner needs the equation of the mirror line.

config.successText: Always give the mirror as an equation: $y = x$, $y = -x$, $x = 0$, $y = 0$. Never words.

slides.title: After a reflection, orientation reverses
slides.prompt: Lengths and angles stay the same (the image is congruent). But the labelling order flips: clockwise becomes anticlockwise.

visual.content:
object · A→B→C clockwise
→
image · A'→B'→C' anticlockwise

slides.title: Rotation: drag the centre, drag the angle
slides.prompt: Three things describe any rotation. A point to spin around, an angle to spin through, and a direction.

slides.title: What three things describe a rotation?

interaction.hint: Where to spin around, how far, which way.

config.prompt: A rotation is fully described by THREE things. They are...

options.whyWrong: Mirror lines are for reflections, not rotations.
Scale factor is for enlargements, not rotations.
Column vectors are for translations. Rotations have a centre, not a vector.

config.successText: Centre + angle + direction. Drop any one and Cambridge takes a mark off.

interaction.hint: Centre is where it spun around. Angle is how far. Direction is which way.

config.prompt: Fill in the three slots from the tiles below.
config.contextHtml: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' style='display:block;width:100%;max-width:420px;height:auto;margin:0 auto;background:#0b1118;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #141e2a' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><defs><pattern id='grl' width='30' height='30' patternUnits='userSpaceOnUse'><path d='M 30 0 L 0 0 0 30' fill='none' stroke='#1a3350' stroke-width='0.5' opacity='0.4'/></pattern></defs><rect width='320' height='200' fill='url(#grl)'/><polygon points='190,140 240,140 215,100' fill='rgba(0,171,250,0.55)' stroke='#00abfa' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='160,170 160,120 120,145' fill='rgba(255,70,112,0.55)' stroke='#ff4670' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='160' cy='170' r='4.5' fill='#fff067' stroke='#0b1118' stroke-width='2'/><path d='M 210 162 A 60 60 0 0 1 156 124' fill='none' stroke='#ff822c' stroke-width='1.3' stroke-dasharray='3 3'/></svg>
config.successText: Rotation, $90°$ anticlockwise, centre $(0, 0)$.

interaction.hint: A full turn is $360°$. Subtract from a full turn to flip direction.

config.prompt: A rotation of $90°$ clockwise gives the same image as which anticlockwise rotation?

options.whyWrong: That's the same magnitude but opposite direction. Image would land in a different place.
$180°$ goes too far. $90°$ clockwise is $90°$ short of a full turn anticlockwise.
That's still clockwise. We need an anticlockwise equivalent.

config.successText: $360° - 90° = 270°$. Cambridge accepts either form.

interaction.hint: $90°$ anticlockwise about the origin: $(x, y) \to (-y, x)$.

config.prompt: Rotating $(3, 0)$ by $90°$ anticlockwise about the origin gives...

options.whyWrong: That's a $180°$ rotation, not $90°$.
That's $90°$ clockwise, the opposite direction.
That's no rotation. The point did move.

interaction.hint: Direction doesn't matter for $180°$. Both signs flip.

config.prompt: A rotation of $180°$ about the origin sends $(x, y)$ to...

options.whyWrong: That's a reflection in $y = x$, not a rotation.
Only $x$ flipped. That's a reflection in the $y$-axis.
Only $y$ flipped. That's a reflection in the $x$-axis.

config.successText: $180°$: both signs flip. The image lands on the opposite side of the centre, same distance away.

slides.title: Three rotations about the origin
slides.prompt: These three coordinate rules cover almost every Cambridge rotation question. Memorise them.

visual.content:
\(90°\) anticlockwise
\((x, y) \to (-y, x)\)
\(180°\) (either way)
\((x, y) \to (-x, -y)\)
\(90°\) clockwise
\((x, y) \to (y, -x)\)

config.prompt: Two students describe the same rotation. Which one earns full marks?

options.whyWrong: No direction. Clockwise or anticlockwise? Mark scheme needs all three.

config.successText: Centre + angle + direction. All three or zero marks.

slides.title: Enlargement: centre and scale factor
slides.prompt: Two things define an enlargement. A point to scale from, and the scale factor.

interaction.hint: Distances from the centre double when $k = 2$.

config.prompt: Drag the pink handle along the ray until the image fills the pink outline. Centre stays at $(0, 0)$, target $k = 2$.
config.successText: $k = 2$: every distance from the centre doubled.

interaction.hint: Three times the distance, three times bigger.

config.prompt: Same centre. This time the image should be three times the size: $k = 3$.
config.successText: Same logic, bigger scale. The shape is similar, just three times larger.

interaction.hint: When the centre is the origin, every coordinate just multiplies by $k$.

config.prompt: Under an enlargement with scale factor $3$ and centre $(0, 0)$, the point $(2, 1)$ maps to...

options.whyWrong: You added $3$ instead of multiplied. Enlargement multiplies, doesn't add.
You only changed one coordinate. Both multiply by $k$.
You swapped the coordinates. That's a reflection in $y = x$, not an enlargement.

config.successText: $(3 \cdot 2,\ 3 \cdot 1) = (6, 3)$. From the origin, every coordinate scales by $k$.

slides.title: Can scale factor be less than 1?

interaction.hint: Distances halve. Image is smaller. Still called an enlargement.

config.prompt: Shrink the image to half size: $k = \tfrac{1}{2}$. Yes, this still counts as an enlargement.
config.successText: $k = \tfrac{1}{2}$ is an enlargement too. The word covers shrinking as well as growing.

interaction.hint: Lengths scale by $k$. Areas scale by $k^2$ — square the scale factor.

config.prompt: After an enlargement with scale factor $\tfrac{1}{2}$, the image area is...

options.text: one quarter of the object area

options.whyWrong: Half is what happens to lengths. Areas use $k^2 = \tfrac{1}{4}$.
Both wrong direction and wrong factor.
Only if $k = 1$. Here $k = \tfrac{1}{2}$, so area must change.

config.successText: Areas scale by $k^2$. $\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \tfrac{1}{4}$. Volume would be $k^3 = \tfrac{1}{8}$.

slides.title: Negative $k$ flips through the centre
slides.prompt: A negative scale factor sends the image to the OPPOSITE side of the centre, then scales it. $k = -2$ is twice the size, on the other side.

interaction.hint: Push the pink handle past the centre to the opposite side.

config.prompt: Place the image so $k = -2$. Twice the size, opposite side of the origin.
config.successText: Negative $k$ flips through the centre AND scales. Both behaviours from one number.

interaction.hint: Type first, then the rule. Scale factor goes before centre.

config.prompt: Arrange the tiles into a proper exam answer.
config.successText: “Enlargement, scale factor $2$, centre $(1, 1)$.” Three pieces, three marks.

slides.title: Combining: do one, then another
slides.prompt: Two transformations in a row. The result is often a different transformation than you'd guess.

interaction.hint: Try translate-then-rotate versus rotate-then-translate. Different landing spots.

config.prompt: When two transformations are applied in sequence, the ORDER of the two...

options.text: matters: doing A then B usually gives a different image than B then A

options.whyWrong: Try rotate $90°$ then translate vs translate then rotate. They land in different places.
Most pairs depend on order. Translations are the special exception.
Order matters across most pairs of transformations.

config.successText: Order almost always matters. Two translations are the one exception (you can add their vectors in either order).

interaction.hint: Two reflections undo the flip. So no flip remains in the final image.

config.prompt: Reflecting in two PARALLEL mirrors is equivalent to...

options.whyWrong: Rotations come from intersecting mirrors, not parallel ones.
Two reflections flip twice — no flip remains.
Sizes don't change under any reflection. No enlargement possible.

config.successText: Two parallel mirrors slide the shape by twice the gap between them. A translation.

interaction.hint: Where the mirrors cross is special — it's the only point both reflections leave alone.

config.prompt: Reflecting in two INTERSECTING mirrors is equivalent to...

options.text: a rotation about the intersection point

options.whyWrong: Translations come from parallel mirrors. Intersecting mirrors give rotation.
Reflections never change size.
The angle is TWICE the angle between the mirrors, not always $180°$.

config.successText: The angle of rotation is twice the angle between the two mirrors.

interaction.hint: $y = 0$ and $y = x$ cross at the origin. Angle between them is $45°$. Double it.

config.prompt: A reflection in $y = 0$ followed by a reflection in $y = x$ is equivalent to...

options.text: a rotation $90°$ anticlockwise about the origin
a rotation $90°$ clockwise about the origin
options.whyWrong: Reversing the mirror order would flip the direction. Here it's $y=0$ first, then $y=x$, which gives anticlockwise.
Parallel mirrors would give a translation. These two mirrors intersect at the origin.
Two reflections never give another reflection. The image flips an even number of times overall.

config.successText: $45°$ between the mirrors. Doubled gives $90°$. Direction is from $y=0$ toward $y=x$: anticlockwise.

slides.title: Two parallel mirrors give a translation

interaction.hint: Vector is twice the perpendicular gap, from the first mirror to the second.

config.prompt: Reflecting in $y = 0$ then in $y = 1$ is equivalent to...

options.whyWrong: Parallel mirrors give a translation, not a rotation.
Two reflections never give a third reflection.
Reflections don't change size, so no enlargement.

config.successText: Gap is $1$ unit, doubled gives $2$. Direction is from $y=0$ up to $y=1$: positive $y$.

slides.title: The decision tree
slides.prompt: Given an object and an image, work through these four questions in order. Each "yes" or "no" narrows it down.

visual.content:
Same size?
NO →
ENLARGEMENT
↓ YES
Orientation flipped?
YES →
REFLECTION
↓ NO
Every vertex shifts by same vector?
YES →
TRANSLATION
↓ NO
ROTATION

interaction.hint: Apply the decision tree: same size? orientation flipped? same shift?

config.prompt: Blue maps to pink. Which transformation is it?
config.contextHtml: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' style='display:block;width:100%;max-width:420px;height:auto;margin:0 auto;background:#0b1118;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #141e2a' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><defs><pattern id='gvt' width='30' height='30' patternUnits='userSpaceOnUse'><path d='M 30 0 L 0 0 0 30' fill='none' stroke='#1a3350' stroke-width='0.5' opacity='0.4'/></pattern></defs><rect width='320' height='200' fill='url(#gvt)'/><polygon points='60,150 100,150 80,110' fill='rgba(0,171,250,0.55)' stroke='#00abfa' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='180,90 220,90 200,50' fill='rgba(255,70,112,0.55)' stroke='#ff4670' stroke-width='1.5'/></svg>

options.whyWrong: Reflection would flip orientation. The triangles point the same way here.
Rotation changes the orientation. Both look the same here.
The triangles are the same size. No enlargement.

config.successText: Same shape, same size, same orientation. That's a translation.

interaction.hint: Pick a vertex on the blue and the matching one on the pink. Count the grid shift.

config.prompt: Same diagram. Which column vector slides blue onto pink?
config.contextHtml: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' style='display:block;width:100%;max-width:420px;height:auto;margin:0 auto;background:#0b1118;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #141e2a' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><defs><pattern id='gvr' width='30' height='30' patternUnits='userSpaceOnUse'><path d='M 30 0 L 0 0 0 30' fill='none' stroke='#1a3350' stroke-width='0.5' opacity='0.4'/></pattern></defs><rect width='320' height='200' fill='url(#gvr)'/><polygon points='60,150 100,150 80,110' fill='rgba(0,171,250,0.55)' stroke='#00abfa' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='180,90 220,90 200,50' fill='rgba(255,70,112,0.55)' stroke='#ff4670' stroke-width='1.5'/></svg>

options.whyWrong: Pink is higher up on the page than blue. Up means positive $y$, not negative.
Negative $x$ means LEFT. Pink is to the RIGHT of blue.
Pink is up-right of blue, so both components are positive.

config.successText: Translation by $\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$. Type plus rule, both correct.

interaction.hint: Reflecting in $y = x$ swaps each coordinate.

config.prompt: Triangle $T$ has vertices $A(1, 1), B(4, 1), C(1, 3)$. Reflect $T$ in $y = x$. Which is the image $T_1$?

options.whyWrong: That's a $180°$ rotation, not a reflection in $y = x$.
That's a reflection in the $x$-axis. Wrong mirror.
That's a reflection in the $y$-axis.

interaction.hint: $90°$ clockwise about the origin: $(x, y) \to (y, -x)$.

config.prompt: Rotate $T_1\ (A_1(1,1), B_1(1,4), C_1(3,1))$ by $90°$ clockwise about the origin. Image $T_2$?

options.whyWrong: That's anticlockwise: $(x,y) \to (-y,x)$. The question asks clockwise.
That's a $180°$ rotation, not $90°$.
That's no rotation. The triangle did rotate $90°$ clockwise.

interaction.hint: Compare each $T$ vertex to its $T_2$ vertex. $x$ stays, $y$ flips sign.

config.prompt: Now describe the SINGLE transformation that maps $T\ (1,1),(4,1),(1,3)$ onto $T_2\ (1,-1),(4,-1),(1,-3)$.

options.whyWrong: $x = 0$ would flip $x$, not $y$. But $x$ is unchanged here.
That flips BOTH signs. Here only $y$ flips.
That swaps coordinates. Here coordinates aren't swapped.

config.successText: Every $y$ has its sign flipped; $x$ stays. That's reflection in the $x$-axis ($y = 0$).

interaction.hint: Type, angle, direction, then centre.

config.prompt: Arrange the four tiles into a proper exam answer.
config.successText: “Rotation, $90°$ anticlockwise, about $(0, 0)$.” Three pieces of information, one clean sentence.

slides.title: You can now describe any single move
slides.prompt: Four transformations. Four mark-scheme patterns. Plus the rules for combining them.
bullets: Name the type first, then give the rule.
Parallel mirrors → translation; intersecting mirrors → rotation.
Two translations → add the column vectors.
Lengths scale by $k$, areas by $k^2$, volumes by $k^3$.
